key_insight: Physics-informed deep learning can predict pixel-level thermal responses of heterogeneous wood more accurately and interpretably than purely data-driven models.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable thermal analysis of wood in architectural and materials engineering workflows, especially when spatial heterogeneity makes homogeneous assumptions fail.
method: PICNNs: add a PDE-based physics loss to CNN training (soft constraint).
PInteCNNs: embed an analytical approximator-predictor-corrector solver inside the CNN (hard constraint).
Use wood RGB images plus testbed temperature maps to predict steady-state thermal fields.
evidence_signal: The approach was validated on three real-world multimodal wood datasets—Poplar, Grandis Cross-Cut, and Grandis Radial-Cut—and compared against data-driven baselines.
watch_item: Physics constraints can improve plausibility, but performance depends on correct PDE formulation and careful integration of noisy experimental measurements.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Modeling for Wood Thermal Analysis and Prediction
